trial_court: Sessions Trial No. 102/2017 by the Additional Sessions Judge, FTC, Durg
case_name: Sunil Dewangan vs The State Of Chhattisgarh

parties.respondent_defendant: The State of Chhattisgarh and Rani Dewangan, non-applicants

facts_of_case: Complainant Rani Dewangan lodged a written complaint alleging physical abuse by applicant Sunil Dewangan on pretext of marriage. She was refused to marry even after birth of one female child in 2016. Charge for offence under Section 376 of IPC was framed against the applicant.

legal_principles.principle: At the stage of framing of charge, the court is not caused to go into valuation of the material available on record.
legal_principles.held: He further submits that at the stage of framing of charge the court is not caused to go into valuation of the material available on record.
cited_cases: Lakesh Kumar Chandradev V. State of Chhattisgarh And Others, (2022) CRMP No. 498
Onkar Nath Mishra And Others V. State (NCT of Delhi) And Another, (2008) 2 Supreme Court Cases 56

legal_principles.principle: The factum of marriage between the parties is a relevant factor to be considered while deciding the charge.
legal_principles.held: Perusal of charge-sheet shows that the present applicant has committed sexual intercourse on 14.02.2015 upon the prosecutrix, thereafter they stayed in hotel in Jagannathpuri where non-applicant No.2 was accepted as wife in a temple by the present applicant.

outcome.final_order: Charge for offence under Section 376 of IPC was framed against the applicant.
